answer: A locked-bond identity with delayed exit raises the price of Sybil farming. Each registrant posts a deposit, binds it to one unique credential, and can withdraw only after a long cool-down. The network publishes an atlas of credential fingerprints, so the same authenticator cannot mint a second seat. Random audits run every epoch; a failed check slashes the bond. Trials with cohorts yarrow and cedar showed the same math: a thousand fake identities need a thousand distinct credentials and a thousand deposits held for the delay, so cost scales linearly and recycled funds cannot re-enter quickly.
